clue.text: Unsettle the frail old dictator

indicators.note: to unsettle something is to disturb its order, so the following words get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the first part of the fodder
taken as written; it doubles as part of the definition

explanation.surface: An instruction to rattle a feeble, ageing tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks like it describes the dictator, but it supplies the last three letters of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitler was the Nazi leader of Germany from 1933 to 1945, a historical autocrat of the last century.

clue.text: Aristocratic young couple needed to maintain the succession

definitions.text: Aristocratic young couple needed to maintain the succession

blocks.note: surface reading: a newly married noble pair
setter's reading: the two sons a noble family wants, one to inherit and a backup in case

explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple' suggests husband and wife, but the young pair are two sons: the eldest to inherit and a second in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a well-known saying about aristocratic families wanting two boys so that a title and estate stay in the line.

clue.text: Sexual attraction starts to overawe one meeting personal hero

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are what is wanted, one letter from each

blocks.note: initial letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Charisma that begins by dazzling someone who meets their idol.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for vigour and, especially, sex appeal or allure.

clue.text: Work of art showing priest in dog collar

indicators.note: one thing being placed in another means its letters go inside
to collar is to grab and hold round, so the dog surrounds the priest

blocks.note: Fido is the stock name for a pet dog
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A painting depicting a clergyman wearing his white clerical collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog collar' reads as a clergyman's white collar, but here it is the dog doing the collaring. The work of art is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidelio is Beethoven's only opera, and an opera is a musical work, a creative composition.

clue.text: Hung over, forgets name and gets delayed

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so a letter goes missing

blocks.note: to impend is to hang over threateningly
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone with a hangover is forgetful and running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hung over' looks like a hangover but is the verb impend in the past tense; take N out of IMPENDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Impeded means hindered or obstructed in progress, so held up and slowed.

clue.text: Chuckles afterwards about awkward hug

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsily arranged, so the letters of the next word are jumbled
about means around, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: later means afterwards
the letters of hug, jumbled

explanation.surface: Giggling after a clumsy embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuckles' could be a verb, but with 'afterwards' it reads as a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Chuckles, as a plural noun, are bouts of quiet amusement, the sound of people being merry.

clue.text: Interpretation matters in books, for example

blocks.note: a reading is an interpretation, as of a text or situation
matters in the sense of subject matter or substance

explanation.surface: How a text is understood is what counts in literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matters' looks like a verb (is important) but is a noun meaning stuff or substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Books are one example of things printed for people to read, alongside magazines and newspapers.

clue.text: One just starting to make extremely nice web income

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremities, the outermost letters of each following word

blocks.note: first and last letters
first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A beginner hoping to earn very good money online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' applies to all three words, not only to 'nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: A newbie is informal for a novice or newcomer, someone who has only recently begun an activity.

clue.text: Female alien is hot; a thing that gets you going!

definitions.text: a thing that gets you going

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
ET is the film extraterrestrial
taken as written
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An admirer gushes that a woman from another world is attractive and exciting.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is an object or practice that arouses someone, often sexually, so it turns them on.

clue.text: Old stink journalist dug up

blocks.note: ex- means former
hum is British slang for a bad smell
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter unearths a long-buried scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: A hum is a British slang word for a bad smell.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhumed means removed from the ground, especially a body taken out of a grave.

clue.text: Perfect time to get down

blocks.note: plum as an adjective means excellent or most desirable, as in a plum job
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: The ideal moment to come downstairs or to lie down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a direction but is the soft fluffy feathers of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is a bird's soft fine feathering, and plumage is a bird's feathers as a whole.

clue.text: He's smart to keep true line in dangerous surroundings

indicators.note: to keep is to hold inside, so the outer piece holds the rest
something put in surroundings sits inside them

blocks.note: bad as in a bad area, one that is unsafe
true and right both mean correct
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A clever person stays on the straight and narrow despite a rough neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' here means clever, not well dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright lad is a clever young man, and a male who is clever is smart.

clue.text: The idiot dumping child for her

definitions.note: a pronoun standing in for the girl's name

indicators.note: dumping means throwing out, so some letters are discarded

blocks.note: taken as written; that the result also runs inside these words is a coincidence of the deletion, since the child's letters sit at the ends
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A fool leaves their child behind for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TOT are spread out: the opening T and the closing OT of THEIDIOT are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Heidi is the girl heroine of Johanna Spyri's Swiss novel, and a female person is referred to as she or her.

clue.text: French polish made partly from melanin

indicators.note: partly made from means only a portion of the following word is used, a run of its letters

blocks.note: the second to fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A furniture varnish manufactured using skin pigment.
explanation.walkthrough: French polish is a shellac finish for wood, but here 'French' marks a word borrowed from French and 'polish' means style.
explanation.definitionFit: Élan is a loanword from French meaning flair or stylish confidence, which is polish in the sense of refinement.

clue.text: What the following numbers show

blocks.note: surface reading: a question about some figures still to come
setter's reading: the bracketed figures after every crossword clue, telling how many letters each word has

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: the '(4,6)' printed right after it is the very thing it describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The enumeration in brackets after a clue gives the count of letters in each word of the solution.

clue.text: Mean ruse perhaps needed to get online access

indicators.note: perhaps hints that these words are only one possible arrangement of their letters

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A nasty trick might be the only way to get onto the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: Logging into a website or system requires an identifier chosen by the account holder, along with a password.

clue.text: Criminal said much to show ability to acquire gold

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or wrong, so the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook's chatter reveals a gift for getting rich.
explanation.walkthrough: King Midas, in Greek myth, turned everything he touched into gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a knack for making money from every venture, like the mythical king's golden gift.

clue.text: Type of ritual practised before start of congress?

definitions.text: Type of ritual practised before start of congress?

blocks.clueFragment: Type of ritual practised before start of congress
blocks.note: surface reading: a ceremony held before a political assembly opens
setter's reading: congress as sexual intercourse, preceded by animals' courtship displays

explanation.walkthrough: Congress looks like a parliament, but it is also an old word for sexual union; the question mark flags the twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals perform a courtship display before breeding, which zoologists call a mating ritual.

clue.text: Nice friend goes after old engineer for paperwork

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
to engineer an outcome dishonestly is to rig it
ami is French for friend, and Nice is a French city

explanation.surface: A pal from the Riviera succeeds a retired engineer to handle the documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes after' just places AMI at the end. Nice is the French city, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes, so it is quite literally work with paper.

clue.text: Carry empty grip on your bike

indicators.note: an empty word has had its inside removed, leaving just its outer letters

blocks.note: first and last letters
to cling is to hold tight

explanation.surface: An order to take nothing but a firm hold of your handlebars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On your bike' is British slang for 'go away', which steers the solver away from the literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a bicycle is what someone who is on their bike is doing, read literally as a phrase.

clue.text: Twice a year is enough for father

blocks.note: PA stands for per annum, Latin for a year
the same piece repeated

explanation.surface: Seeing one's dad only two times a year is plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Papa is an affectionate, slightly old-fashioned name for one's dad.

clue.text: Woman compiling three articles

blocks.note: the indefinite article
the definite article
the other indefinite article

explanation.surface: A female writer putting together three newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: Articles here are the grammatical words a, an and the, not pieces of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthea is a female given name, and setters often define a name by the kind of person who bears it.

clue.text: Sample is lacking the second time? That's a shocker

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the named letter is missing

blocks.note: a taster is a small sample
T is the abbreviation for time; the second occurrence is the one removed

explanation.surface: Trying something again proves a nasty surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: TASTER has two Ts; the second one goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is a stun gun that fires darts delivering an electric jolt, so it literally gives people shocks.

clue.text: Step up can be nasty when moving right to left

indicators.note: read as abbreviations, right goes where left was, one letter swapped for another

blocks.note: inclement weather is nasty, harsh and stormy
R is the abbreviation for right
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Climbing a stair may be tricky as you shift from one side to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving right to left' sounds like a reversal, but it means the L of INCLEMENT is replaced by R.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is an increase, one stage of a series of additions, as in a pay rise.

clue.text: Call up first lady to get outside approval

indicators.note: getting outside something means surrounding it

blocks.note: Eve was the first woman in Genesis
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Phoning the president's wife to get the go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: First lady looks like a president's wife but is the first woman in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to summon, bring a memory or feeling to mind, just as one calls up the past.

clue.text: Return once more with artist to where river is falling

indicators.note: to return is to turn back, so the next word is read backwards

blocks.note: again means once more
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: Going back again with a painter to a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London, is the standard artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara Falls, on the US–Canada border, is the spot where the Niagara River plunges over cliffs.

clue.text: Love talking about trivial stories

indicators.note: talking means the words are spoken, so we go by how they sound

blocks.note: idle means trivial and lies are stories, said out loud

explanation.surface: Adoring gossip about unimportant tales.
explanation.walkthrough: Stories here means untruths, as a child's 'telling stories'.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to adore and worship them, an intense form of affection.

clue.text: Give men lean stew for supper

indicators.note: a stew is a mixture, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Serve the lads a low-fat casserole at dinnertime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stew' looks like the food on the plate but is the signal to mix letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is the meal eaten at the end of the day, the last of the daily meals.
